brief: 6 rebrand mistakes that cost startups their best customers.

slots.headline: Six rebrand mistakes that kill customer loyalty
slots.swipeNote: Swipe to see all six costly mistakes

slots.title: Chasing trends over truth
slots.body: Startups often mimic competitors to look relevant, but borrowed aesthetics signal insecurity. Customers sense the disconnect and lose trust fast.

slots.title: Ignoring your loyal fans
slots.body: A rebrand built only for new audiences alienates the community that built you. Exclusion feels like betrayal to early believers.

slots.title: Overcomplicating the visual system
slots.body: Abstract logos and clever gradients look impressive in decks but confuse users at checkout. Clarity always beats cleverness.

slots.title: Inconsistent rollout across channels
slots.body: When your app, site, and emails look like different companies, trust crumbles. A rebrand is only as strong as its execution.

slots.title: Erasing hard-won search equity
slots.body: Changing your name and URLs without a migration plan destroys organic traffic. Visibility lost overnight can take years to rebuild.

slots.title: Rebranding without internal buy-in
slots.body: If your team cannot articulate the new story, neither can your customers. Culture must change before the logo does.

slots.quote: Your brand is a promise, not a paint job
slots.headline: Build a rebrand that keeps customers
slots.author: By the Vantage team
